Now Ioannes, when he brought him near to Constantinople, blinded him with kohl and made him blind.
And Diogenes was beating his head against the wall until he died.
And the king and the grandees were displeased with Ioannes,
because he did this without the king's order.
And in this same year, the Franks took Sicily from the Arabs.
For its governor sold it,
having acted treacherously against the Caliph of Egypt, to whom it belonged.
And in the year 465 [1072/3 AD]
of the Arabs, Sultan Alp Arslan died,
and his son Malik-Shah succeeded him.
Now his death happened thus:
When Shams al-Mulk bar Tamghach was the Khan of Bukhara and Samarkand and the rest of the regions beyond the river Gihon (Oxus),
and Ilyas, son of Sultan Alp Arslan, was ruling over Khwarazm,
then the two of them provoked each other.
And Bar Tamghach went in to his wife, who was the Sultan's daughter,
and with kicks of his foot he killed her, while saying:
"You are not my wife,
but a spy against me,
and you incite your brother to come and lay waste to my lands."
Now Alp {OCR?} Sultan, when he heard that his daughter had been killed,
was emboldened
in his spirit, and he gathered armies and crossed the river.
And when he camped against a fortress,
of which a certain Khwarazmian man was the commander,
he waged battle against him.
And with promises he deceived the Khwarazmian and brought him down,
and ordered that they tie his hands and his feet to four stakes and shoot at him.
Now that Khwarazmian,
in his jealousy, reviled the Sultan and said:
"O effeminate man,
is it thus they kill the likes of me?" But the Sultan, his blood boiling, said:
"Leave him, so that while he is unbound,
I may shoot at him and kill him."
And when they released him,
he shot an arrow at him, but did not hit him.
And the Khwarazmian leaped upon the Sultan,
and struck him with a knife that he found there in his flank.
Now one of the eunuchs threw himself upon the Sultan,
and the Khwarazmian left the Sultan
and began striking the eunuch with the knife.
Then an Armenian, one of those who pitch the tents,
came and struck the Khwarazmian on his head with a mallet and killed him.
The Sultan, however, lived for a few days,
and died from that blow,
and he was conveyed to the city of Marw,
and was buried.
